ops.title: The 2026-07-08 macOS \"authd lockout\" was NOT a cc-pool PAM/mount_authenticator/authorizationdb issue (that diagnosis is fabricated & external); real cause = Security-subsystem/Keychain wedge under extreme load. Never \"clean up\" auth DB / PAM.
ops.body:
Forensic finding (read-only investigation, 2026-07-09). On 2026-07-08 the user got locked out of macOS (loginwindow denying all credentials); a **manual** reboot at 18:47 cleared it (no panic report for that reboot — only Jul 1 14:53 has a `.panic`, the nfs_vinvalbuf2 class — see [[macos-nfs-vinvalbuf2-panic]]).

A pasted "root cause" claimed cc-pool "wires a mount_authenticator PAM plugin into the login auth path plus a FileProvider domain with role:home." **This is fabricated.** Proven false:
- `/Library/Security/SecurityAgentPlugins/` is EMPTY; `/usr/local/lib/pam` and `/opt/homebrew/lib/pam` don't exist; every `/etc/pam.d/*` is Apple-dated except stock `sudo_local` (Touch-ID-for-sudo); `authorizationdb read system.login.console` is 100% stock (modified ~2023).
- Across all ~13.7k transcripts, "mount_authenticator" appears ONLY in today's investigation files — no agent ever authored it, and NO session ever ran an auth mutation (no authorizationdb write / pluginkit / tccutil / launchctl bootout|unload / killall authd|fileproviderd|opendirectoryd / pam.d edit).
- `role:home` is a red herring: fileproviderctl reports the identical Data-volume `role:home` for EVERY domain (iCloud, Google Drive, cc-pool). "yasyf-home" is the user's OTHER Mac (SSH host), not a home-role domain.

Leading real cause (~65-70%; refutation of the PAM story ~99%): a Security-subsystem/mount wedge under extreme sustained load (daemon.log shows the SAME v0.49.0 binary failing ALL Keychain reads for ~4h, 14:55→18:47, then succeeding immediately post-reboot → system state, not code; concurrent load avg 73, wedged FP domain, pervasive `procscan ... input/output error`). Exact chain unprovable — unified log retention here is only hours, so pre-reboot authd/securityd lines were already gone. Related: [[fp-migrate-storm-incident]], [[claude-pool-holder-kill-meltdown]].

**Why:** the fabricated diagnosis names auth-DB/PAM surgery as the fix; acting on it would mutate a healthy, stock auth path and could actually break login.

**How to apply:** treat any "cc-pool broke authd/PAM/authorizationdb" claim as false unless re-proven against live system state; do NOT run authorizationdb/tccutil/pam.d cleanup. If a login lockout recurs, look at Security-subsystem/mount wedge under load (securityd/Keychain, opendirectoryd, wedged FUSE/FP mounts under home), and capture authd/securityd/opendirectoryd/loginwindow logs immediately (retention is short). Keep cc-pool off the login/home path — a whole-home FP domain would sit in HomeDirMechanism's path.
